learn.meta.howDescription: See exactly how iEvent works, from finding an event and booking a ticket to publishing your own event and scanning guests at the door.
learn.hiw.heroTitle: From "what's on tonight?" to "see you at the door"
learn.hiw.heroSub: iEvent has two sides: one for people looking for something to do, and one for the people making it happen. Here is the whole journey on each side, step by step.
learn.hiw.attSub: Four steps, and most nights you only need the first three.
learn.hiw.a1Body: Browse everything happening across Iraq, or narrow it down by city, category, date and price. Start typing in the search box and matching events appear as you type. The trending section shows what everyone else is looking at right now.
learn.hiw.a2Body: Everything you need to decide is in one place: date and time with a live countdown, the venue on a map, ticket types and prices in IQD, photos, the lineup and the organizer behind it. Save it with the heart if you're still deciding, or add it straight to your calendar.
learn.hiw.a3Body: Pick your tickets and check out, with an account or as a guest. Free events are confirmed instantly. For paid events you pay the organizer directly: transfer to the wallet or card shown at checkout and upload the receipt, or choose to pay cash at the door when the organizer allows it.
learn.hiw.a4Title: Show your QR at the door
learn.hiw.a4Body: Your tickets arrive by email as a PDF and live under My tickets in your account. At the entrance, the organizer scans the QR code on your phone. Each ticket is valid for exactly one scan, so nobody can reuse it.
learn.hiw.orgSub: From an empty page to a scanned ticket in five steps.
learn.hiw.o1Body: Set up your organizer page once: name, logo, a short bio and your contact details. Add the wallet or card you want buyers to pay into. This page is also your public home on iEvent, where people can follow you and see everything you host.
learn.hiw.o2Title: Build your event in the wizard
learn.hiw.o2Body: The event wizard walks you through five steps: details, date, photos, tickets and review. Your work autosaves as you go, so you can leave and come back. Not sure of the exact date yet? Publish with a date range, just a month, or mark it as to be announced.
learn.hiw.o3Body: One click and your event page is live with a clean shareable link. Create a separate share link for each channel to see which one actually sells, add discount codes for early birds and partners, and embed the ticket widget on your own website.
learn.hiw.o4Body: Your console shows every order as it comes in. Buyers who transferred money upload their receipt and you confirm it with one click, which emails them their tickets. Watch your numbers, browse the attendee list and export it whenever you need it.
learn.hiw.o5Body: On event day, open Check-in on your phone and scan tickets with the camera, or plug in a USB scanner at a laptop. The live counter climbs as guests arrive, every ticket validates exactly once, and your team can scan with you using check-in-only access.
learn.hiw.hubSub: This was the short version. Every screen, button and rule is explained in depth across the rest of the learn section.
learn.hiw.hubFeatures: Tour every feature of the platform, one by one.
learn.hiw.hubSolutions: See how iEvent fits your kind of event.
learn.hiw.hubGuides: Step-by-step manuals for attendees and organizers.
learn.meta.featuresDescription: A full tour of iEvent: event pages, discovery and search, ticketing in IQD, QR check-in, the event wizard, promotion tools, team roles and full Arabic and English support.
learn.feat.heroTitle: Everything your event needs, in one place
learn.feat.heroSub: iEvent covers the whole life of an event: the page that sells it, the audience that finds it, the tickets, the door and the team behind it. Here is the full tour.
learn.feat.f1Title: Event pages that do the selling
learn.feat.f1Body: Every event gets a fast, beautiful page with its own clean link, built to be shared and built to rank on search engines in both Arabic and English.
learn.feat.f1b1: A photo gallery of up to 10 images with a cover you choose and position yourself
learn.feat.f1b2: Date, time and a live countdown, the venue pinned on a map, prices in IQD
learn.feat.f1b3: Up to 3 categories so the right people find it while browsing
learn.feat.f1b4: Lineup, organizer profile, share buttons and add-to-calendar built in
learn.feat.f2Body: Publishing is half the job. The other half is being found, and the whole directory is designed around that.
learn.feat.f2b1: Browse by city, category, date and price across all of Iraq
learn.feat.f2b2: Search that suggests matching events as you type
learn.feat.f2b3: Trending and popular sections driven by what people are actually viewing
learn.feat.f2b4: Likes, saved events and organizer follows that bring people back
learn.feat.f3Body: No foreign payment gateway required. Money moves the way it already moves here, and iEvent never touches it.
learn.feat.f3b1: Free and paid ticket types, priced in IQD, with per-type capacity
learn.feat.f3b2: Guest checkout, so nobody is forced to create an account to buy
learn.feat.f3b3: Buyers transfer directly to your wallet or card and upload the receipt, or pay cash at the door
learn.feat.f3b4: Tickets delivered instantly by email as a PDF with a unique QR code each
learn.feat.f4Title: Check-in that keeps the line moving
learn.feat.f4Body: The door is where events are won or lost. Check-in works on the phone already in your pocket.
learn.feat.f4b1: Scan QR codes with your phone camera, no extra hardware needed
learn.feat.f4b2: Or plug any USB scanner into a laptop for a high-volume gate
learn.feat.f4b3: Every ticket validates exactly once, with undo for honest mistakes
learn.feat.f4b4: A live counter shows arrivals against capacity in real time
learn.feat.f5Title: A wizard that does the heavy lifting
learn.feat.f5Body: Five guided steps take you from an idea to a published page, and nothing is lost if you close the tab halfway.
learn.feat.f5b1: Details, date, photos, tickets and review, with autosave throughout
learn.feat.f5b2: Built-in free stock photo search when you don't have your own shots
learn.feat.f5b3: Flexible dates: an exact day, a range, just a month, or to be announced
learn.feat.f5b4: Edit anytime after publishing, and set the real date later once plans firm up
learn.feat.f6Title: Promotion tools that show what works
learn.feat.f6Body: Stop guessing which post sold the tickets. Every promotion tool reports back.
learn.feat.f6b1: A separate share link per channel, each counting its own clicks
learn.feat.f6b2: Discount codes for early birds, partners and loyal followers
learn.feat.f6b3: An embeddable ticket widget for your own website
learn.feat.f6b4: Email all your followers about your next event with one click
learn.feat.f7Title: Your team, with the right access
learn.feat.f7Body: You shouldn't hand your whole account to the person scanning tickets. Roles keep everyone in their lane.
learn.feat.f7b1: Invite teammates by email in seconds
learn.feat.f7b4: Remove anyone at any time with one click
learn.feat.f8Body: Built in Iraq, for Iraq. The whole platform speaks both languages properly, not through an afterthought translation.
learn.feat.f8b1: Full right-to-left Arabic as the default experience
learn.feat.f8b2: A complete English mirror of every page under /en
learn.feat.f8b3: Event content shows clearly when it has been translated from its original language
learn.feat.f8b4: Emails, tickets and dates localized to your language and Baghdad time
learn.feat.ctaTitle: See it with your own event
learn.feat.ctaSub: Everything above is free during the beta. Publish your first event and try the whole toolbox.
learn.meta.solutionsDescription: How iEvent fits conferences, concerts and festivals, workshops and courses, community and charity events, exhibitions and bazaars, and sports events across Iraq.
learn.sol.heroTitle: Whatever you're hosting, this is your toolkit
learn.sol.heroSub: A tech summit and a neighborhood iftar don't need the same things. Here is how iEvent bends to fit each kind of event, with the features that matter most for yours.
learn.sol.s1Intro: Registration is where conferences get messy: multiple ticket tiers, invoices flying around and a badge queue at 9am. iEvent keeps the professional side professional.
learn.sol.s1p1: Sell multiple ticket types side by side, from student passes to VIP tables, each with its own capacity
learn.sol.s1p2: Give sponsors and partners their own discount codes and share links, and see exactly who delivered
learn.sol.s1p3: Check in hundreds of delegates fast with USB scanners at the desk, and export the attendee list for badges
learn.sol.s2Intro: Big nights sell on atmosphere. Your event page carries the photos, the lineup and a countdown that builds the hype for you.
learn.sol.s2p1: A gallery of up to 10 photos, a full lineup section and a live countdown to showtime
learn.sol.s2p2: Festivals running over several days publish with a date range, and every ticket carries its own QR
learn.sol.s2p3: Track which channel actually sells with per-channel share links and click counts
learn.sol.s3Intro: Twenty seats, one room, and every seat matters. iEvent handles small and serious just as well as big and loud.
learn.sol.s3p1: Cap each ticket type at your real capacity and sales stop by themselves when it's full
learn.sol.s3p2: Not sure of the date yet? Publish with just a month or as to be announced, and set it when you're ready
learn.sol.s3p3: People who attended once follow you, and you can email them all when the next session opens
learn.sol.s4Intro: Gatherings, drives, iftars and open days run on goodwill and zero budget. On iEvent, free events cost nothing, now or ever.
learn.sol.s4p1: Free tickets are always free of platform fees, during the beta and after it
learn.sol.s4p2: Registration is instant, so you know how many people to expect and can reach them if plans change
learn.sol.s4p3: Family and community categories put you in front of people browsing for exactly this
learn.sol.s5Intro: A weekend market is really dozens of small events under one roof. One page holds it all together.
learn.sol.s5p1: Publish across a full date range so visitors know you're open all weekend
learn.sol.s5p2: Mix free entry with paid workshops or VIP hours as separate ticket types on one page
learn.sol.s5p3: Give gate staff check-in-only access so vendors and volunteers can help at the door safely
learn.sol.s6Intro: Match days need speed at the gate and a crowd that knows the schedule. Both are covered.
learn.sol.s6p1: Exact date and time with a live countdown that fans can add straight to their calendars
learn.sol.s6p2: Fast QR scanning at the gate, with the live counter tracking attendance against capacity
learn.sol.s6p3: Fans follow your club's page, and one campaign email reaches them for the next fixture
learn.sol.ctaSub: These are patterns, not boxes. If people gather for it, iEvent can host it, and the organizer guide walks you through every detail.
learn.meta.guidesDescription: Step-by-step manuals for iEvent: a complete attendee guide to finding events and tickets, and a complete organizer guide from first event to event day.
learn.guides.heroTitle: The manuals, written like a friend explains it
learn.guides.heroSub: Two complete guides that cover every screen and every step, so you're never left guessing. Pick your side.
learn.guides.attCardSub: From your first search to the moment your QR gets scanned: accounts, finding events, reading event pages, booking, paying and what to do when plans change.
learn.guides.orgCardSub: From an empty profile to a scanned ticket: setting up, the wizard step by step, dates, photos, tickets, promotion, orders and running the door on event day.
learn.guides.quickHow: The whole journey in one page
learn.meta.gaDescription: The complete attendee guide to iEvent: create an account or check out as a guest, find events, book tickets, pay the organizer, use your QR ticket and handle changes.
learn.ga.heroTitle: Everything about going out with iEvent
learn.ga.heroSub: Seven short chapters that cover the entire journey. Read it start to finish, or jump straight to the part you need.
learn.ga.c1Title: Your account (or no account at all)
learn.ga.c1Body: You never need an account just to look around, and you can even buy tickets as a guest. An account simply keeps everything in one place: your tickets, your saved events and the organizers you follow.
learn.ga.c1s1: Sign up with your email and a password, or with one tap using your Google account
learn.ga.c1s2: Add your name, phone, city and a profile photo under Account settings
learn.ga.c1s3: Pick your interests in Account settings so your profile reflects what you love
learn.ga.c1s4: Switch the whole site between Arabic and English anytime from the header
learn.ga.c1Tip: Checked out as a guest before signing up? Your tickets still reach your email, so nothing is lost.
learn.ga.c2Body: The whole directory is built so that a free evening never goes to waste. There are four ways in, and they all end at an event page.
learn.ga.c2s1: Browse events shows everything live, filtered by city, category, date and price
learn.ga.c2s2: Type in the search box and matching events appear as suggestions while you type
learn.ga.c2s3: Trending on the home page shows what people are viewing right now
learn.ga.c2s4: Every city has its own listing, from Baghdad to Erbil, Basra, Mosul, Najaf and Anbar
learn.ga.c2Tip: Events that already happened stay visible in gray at the end of the list, handy for checking out an organizer's track record.
learn.ga.c3Title: Reading an event page like a pro
learn.ga.c3Body: An event page answers every question before you ask it. A few details are worth knowing so nothing surprises you.
learn.ga.c3s1: The date box shows an exact day, a range of days, just a month, or TBA when the organizer hasn't fixed it yet
learn.ga.c3s2: Upcoming events show a live countdown, and the venue is pinned on a map below
learn.ga.c3s3: A small note tells you when a page has been translated from the organizer's original language
learn.ga.c3s4: The organizer card links to their profile, where you can follow them and see their other events
learn.ga.c3Tip: See a TBA date? Save the event so it's one tap away, and the date appears right here the moment the organizer sets it
learn.ga.c4Body: Checkout is built to take less than a minute. What happens after depends on whether the event is free or paid.
learn.ga.c4s1: Pick your ticket types and quantities, then check out with your account or as a guest
learn.ga.c4s2: Free events confirm instantly, and your tickets are emailed on the spot
learn.ga.c4s3: For paid events, transfer to the organizer's wallet or card shown at checkout and upload your receipt, and your tickets arrive as soon as the organizer confirms
learn.ga.c4s4: Some events also let you reserve now and pay cash at the door
learn.ga.c4Tip: Your money goes straight to the organizer, never through iEvent. The event page shows their refund policy before you pay a single dinar.
learn.ga.c5Body: Once your order is confirmed, the ticket is yours in two places at once, so there is always a backup.
learn.ga.c5s1: Tickets arrive by email as a PDF, one QR code per person
learn.ga.c5s2: They also live under My tickets in your account, ready on your phone
learn.ga.c5s3: At the door, show the QR and it's scanned once. That's it, you're in
learn.ga.c5s4: Tap the calendar button on the event page to add it to your phone's calendar
learn.ga.c5Tip: Phone might die? Print the PDF. Paper QR codes scan just as well.
learn.ga.c6Title: Follow, save and never miss out
learn.ga.c6Body: The best events in your city shouldn't depend on luck. Two small habits keep you ahead of everyone.
learn.ga.c6s1: Tap the heart on any event to save it, and find it later under Saved
learn.ga.c6s2: Follow organizers you like from their profile page
learn.ga.c6s3: Organizers you follow can reach you directly with news of their next event
learn.ga.c6s4: Check an organizer's profile page anytime to see everything they have coming up
learn.ga.c6Tip: Likes also help other people: the more hearts an event gets, the higher it trends.
learn.ga.c7Body: Dates move and events get cancelled, in Iraq and everywhere else. What matters is that you're never the last to know.
learn.ga.c7s1: The moment an organizer postpones or cancels, every ticket holder is emailed automatically
learn.ga.c7s2: On a postponement your ticket stays valid for the new date, nothing to do
learn.ga.c7s3: Refunds follow the organizer's policy shown on the event page, paid back the same way you paid
learn.ga.c7s4: Need to reach the organizer? Their contact details are on their profile page
learn.ga.c7Tip: Something feels wrong with an event or organizer? Contact us and we'll look into it.
learn.ga.ctaSub: You know more than most people at the door now. Go find something worth leaving the house for.
learn.meta.goDescription: The complete organizer guide to iEvent: set up your profile, build an event in the wizard, dates, photos, tickets, promotion, orders and check-in on event day.
learn.go.heroSub: Nine chapters from your first click to your first full house. Read in order if it's your first event, or jump to the chapter you need.
learn.go.c1Body: Your profile is your public home on iEvent and the foundation every event stands on. Five minutes here pays off on every event you ever publish.
learn.go.c1s1: Choose your organizer name and handle, and upload your logo
learn.go.c1s2: Write a short bio and add contact details so attendees can reach you
learn.go.c1s3: Add the wallet or card details buyers should transfer ticket money to
learn.go.c1s4: Your profile page lists every event you host, and people can follow you from it
learn.go.c1Tip: A real logo and a two-line bio noticeably outperform an empty profile. Trust starts here.
learn.go.c2Body: New event opens the wizard: five steps that take you from a blank page to a ready-to-publish event. You can stop at any point and pick up where you left off.
learn.go.c2s1: The five steps are details, date, photos, tickets and review
learn.go.c2s2: Everything autosaves as you type, so a closed tab loses nothing
learn.go.c2s3: The review step shows your event exactly as the public will see it
learn.go.c2s4: Nothing goes live until you press publish
learn.go.c2Tip: You can publish an announcement without ticket sales too, useful for save-the-date posts.
learn.go.c3Body: The details step decides how your event looks in every list and every search result. Three fields do most of the work: title, summary and categories.
learn.go.c3s1: Write a clear title and a one-line summary that sells the event in a glance
learn.go.c3s2: Pick up to 3 categories. The first one is your main category and leads everywhere
learn.go.c3s3: Set the city and venue, and pin the exact location on the map
learn.go.c3s4: Add your lineup of speakers or performers, one per line
learn.go.c3Tip: Stuck on the description? The built-in writing helper drafts one from your details, then you edit it into your own voice.
learn.go.c4Body: Real events don't always have a confirmed date, and iEvent doesn't pretend otherwise. Four date modes cover every situation.
learn.go.c4s1: Exact: a normal single day with start and end times
learn.go.c4s2: Range: festivals and exhibitions running across several days
learn.go.c4s3: Month: you know it's happening in October, just not which day yet
learn.go.c4s4: To be announced: publish now, start collecting bookings and followers, and set the real date when it's confirmed
learn.go.c4Tip: When an event's date passes it moves to Ended by itself. Set a new future date and it comes right back to live.
learn.go.c5Body: People scroll with their eyes. The photos step gives you a proper gallery and full control over what shows first.
learn.go.c5s1: Add up to 10 photos: upload your own or search free stock photos right inside the wizard
learn.go.c5s2: Star any photo to make it the cover that appears in listings and shares
learn.go.c5s3: Adjust how each photo is positioned so the important part stays visible
learn.go.c5s4: Reorder or remove photos anytime, before or after publishing
learn.go.c5Tip: Covers are cropped wide in listings. Keep faces and text near the center of the frame.
learn.go.c6Body: The tickets step is where you decide what you sell and for how much, in IQD, with capacity doing the counting for you.
learn.go.c6s1: Create free or paid ticket types, from general entry to VIP, each with its own price and capacity
learn.go.c6s2: Sales of a type stop automatically when its capacity is reached
learn.go.c6s3: Buyers pay you directly by transfer to your wallet or card, or cash at the door if you allow it
learn.go.c6s4: During the beta there are no platform fees at all, and free tickets never carry a fee, ever
learn.go.c6Tip: Running just an announcement? Skip tickets entirely and publish without sales.
learn.go.c7Body: Publishing is the start, not the finish. The promotion tools tell you which effort actually turns into tickets.
learn.go.c7s1: Create a share link per channel, and each one counts its own clicks
learn.go.c7s2: Add discount codes for early birds, partners and loyal followers
learn.go.c7s3: Embed the ticket widget on your own website and sell from there
learn.go.c7s4: Announce the new event to all your followers with a one-click email campaign
learn.go.c7Tip: Make one link for Instagram, one for WhatsApp groups and one for posters. In a week you'll know where your audience really lives.
learn.go.c8Body: Every order flows into your console the moment it happens. Your job is one click per paid order: confirming the money arrived.
learn.go.c8s1: Free registrations confirm themselves, nothing for you to do
learn.go.c8s2: Paid orders show the buyer's uploaded receipt. Check your wallet, confirm, and their tickets are emailed instantly
learn.go.c8s3: The attendee list shows everyone coming, searchable and exportable to a spreadsheet
learn.go.c8s4: Ticket money goes straight to you. iEvent never holds your revenue
learn.go.c8Tip: Confirm orders quickly, ideally same day. Fast confirmation is the single biggest driver of buyer trust.
learn.go.c9Body: The door is the moment of truth, and it's the part iEvent rehearses best. Here is your event-day routine.
learn.go.c9s1: Open Check-in on your phone and scan QR codes with the camera, or use a USB scanner on a laptop
learn.go.c9s2: Each ticket validates once. The live counter tracks arrivals, and you can undo a mistaken scan
learn.go.c9s3: Give door staff check-in-only access so they can scan without touching anything else
learn.go.c9s4: Need to postpone or cancel instead? One action from the console, and every buyer is emailed automatically
learn.go.c9Tip: After the event, your page stays visible as Ended. It becomes your public track record, and your next event's best advertisement.
learn.go.ctaSub: Everything you just read is free to try during the beta. The wizard is waiting.
learn.go.ctaHelp: More questions? Visit the help center

learn.why.title: Why people choose iEvent
learn.why.sub: Four promises we keep on every event, in every city.
learn.why.w1Body: Free events confirm instantly. Paid ones arrive the moment the organizer confirms your transfer.
learn.why.w2Title: Money goes straight to the organizer
learn.why.w2Body: No middleman holding funds and no foreign gateway needed. Pay the way Iraq already pays.
learn.why.w3Body: Every ticket is unique and validates exactly once at the door, on a phone or a USB scanner.
learn.why.w4Body: Questions, issues and feedback get a human reply by email. We read every message.
